newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end 1/8 to 1/4 higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end 1/8 to 1/4 higher.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices ended 1/8 to 1/4 point higher Thursday in a session one trader said drew the first noteworthy nibbles from retail investors in recent weeks.
"It feels like for the first time in a few weeks the market has got kind of a decent retail bid," the trader said.
A paucity of fresh municipal supply and a U.S. Treasury market that has come off it's lows appear to have whetted retail's appetite, he said.

"I'd say on some of the retail stuff yields are down three or four basis points, but the market in general is probably up 1/8 to 1/4," the trader said. "And it's got a decent tone for the first time in a while."

A municipal analyst also pegged the broader market up 1/8 to 1/4 point. High-grade issues firmed slightly, while dollar bonds finished up 1/4 point. Dollar bonds had been up 1/4 point in the morning and faded to flat by noon (EST), but managed a late-session rebound, he said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed up 8/32 at 114-12/32. The March T-bond contract closed up 10/32 at 110-18/32. The MOB spread was 122 ticks.
The government's 30-year bond ended up 15/32 at 95-10/32 to yield 6.87 percent.

Turning to new issues, Bear Stearns & Co won $44 million Lowell, Mass., state qualified municipal purpose loan of 1997 limited tax bonds, Thursday's biggest deal. Bear Stearns won at a true interest cost of 5.38 percent.

Next week's new issue slate also appears thin so far, with just $1.56 billion of negotiated and competitive debt expected. Negotiated deals are expected to number 23 and total $1.280 billion next week.
The biggest is expected to be a $459 million Anaheim Public Finance Authority, Calif., offering via PaineWebber Inc on Tuesday.

Anaheim PFA is also slated to sell a $59 million taxable issue through PaineWebber that day. Proceeds are slated to fund improvements to areas surrounding the Disneyland resort and to the city's convention center.
Next week's competitive issues are expected to number 42 and total $280 million. The largest is expected to be a $30 million Fresno Unified School District, Calif., deal on Thursday.
